sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: Fourth of 6 case-study docs (3a–3f). Same format as 3a–3c v1.

Topic 2.2 has 9 case-study slots from the syllabus: factors in weathering, mass movement and fluvial processes; karst features, formation and ecosystem services; fluvial features, delta formation and delta ecosystem services. The syllabus has no strategy points here, so there are no succeeded/failed pairs. 10 pages.
Built with tools/build_case_studies.py from tools/data/case_studies_3d.json; charts 2_2_*.png; checked with tools/check_docx.py.

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: Landform cases (Ha Long Bay, Son Doong, Majuli) are places rather than single events; each uses post-2015 data or decisions (e.g. 2023 World Heritage extension, 2016 satellite area).
Process explanations (carbonation, shear stress vs strength, braiding conditions) are standard syllabus knowledge, not taken from the listed sources.
Same limits as before: no photos, and figures come from search results quoting each source.

rows: Deaths 231 (NHESS) vs 238 in another report; landslides 269 vs 370+.
'600+ ha lost a year' is one expert's estimate; 114 Mt is licensed sand only.
1,133 islands (UNESCO) — some sources say about 1,600 or 1,969.
Permits vary by year (500 in 2015, about 800 in 2017); price about US$3,000.
1,256 → 524 km² (1971–2016, Dialogue Earth) vs 629 → 487 km² (1975–2024, EGU25) — different baselines.
Most figures come from advocacy sources (HRW, 350.org); '2.5 million people' is HRW's estimate.
Angkor's temples (cultural site). Alternative: deep weathering profiles in Singapore's granite.
Braided Brahmaputra only; meanders are mentioned as a contrast. A meander case (e.g. a Mekong or Amazon loop) could be added.
Sundarbans. Alternative: Mekong Delta rice and aquaculture (overlaps slot 8).
